name: Obsidian Sync
tagline: Paid sync service for a local-first Markdown knowledge base

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; Sync listed at $5/user/month monthly and $4/user/month annually.
pricing.freeTier: Sync itself has no free tier, though the Obsidian app is free.

verdictSummary: If you already accept local Markdown files, syncing folders across devices is a solved problem; the hard part is not the app, it is conflict-free convenience.
coreLoopDIY: Use a local Markdown folder, git/Syncthing/iCloud/Drive for sync, and optional scripts for backlinks/search.
requirements: Syncthing, Git, iCloud, Dropbox, or similar
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay for no-drama sync across devices while keeping Obsidian's local-first model.

priorArt.name: Syncthing
priorArt.desc: Open-source continuous file synchronization that can replace much of Obsidian Sync for tec

alternatives.name: iCloud Drive
alternatives.desc: Five free gigabytes and excellent Apple plumbing; everyone else gets a side door.

alternatives.name: Nextcloud
alternatives.desc: Your own cloud, complete with the privilege of maintaining your own cloud.

alternatives.name: Syncthing
alternatives.desc: Syncs the vault directly between computers; iPhones remain the awkward relative.

notes: Very clean yes; lets the site distinguish app value from convenience subscription.
prompt:
Build me a sync setup for my Obsidian vault to replace Obsidian Sync. Requirements:

- This is plumbing, not an app: the vault is a folder of Markdown files, sync it with
  git. Syncthing is the zero-history alternative; use git here because I want history.
- A small watcher (Node + chokidar + simple-git, or a plain bash script on a
  systemd/launchd timer, pick the simpler) that debounces 30 seconds after the last
  change, commits with an auto message, and pushes to a private GitHub repo.
- On start and every 5 minutes: pull with rebase. On conflict, never lose data: write
  the incoming version as <name>.conflict-YYYY-MM-DD.md, keep mine in place, and log it.
- .gitignore for .obsidian/workspace* and .trash so device-local state does not ping-
  pong between machines.
- A `vaultsync status` command showing last push/pull time and any outstanding conflict
  files.
- Mobile: point a git client (Working Copy on iOS, MGit on Android) at the same repo.
  Document that in the README, do not build mobile anything.
- The repo stays private; token in .env or the system git credential helper. No accounts
  beyond GitHub, no telemetry, notes stay plain Markdown on disk.
- Out of scope: an encrypted-vault workflow and a version-history UI. git log is the
  history.
- README: second-machine setup steps and the conflict-file convention.
